MECHANISM ESTABLISHED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE, and it is the GC side of the fork, not CDP dropping the evaluation. In V8 branch 14.9-lkgr, which is what Chromium 149 ships (installed browser reports 149.0.7827.55, chromiumdash maps mstone 149 to v8_branch 14.9), ProtocolPromiseHandler's constructor calls m_evaluationResult.SetWeak unconditionally, with no guard. So every Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise true holds the awaited promise through a weak v8::Global for its whole pending life; if nothing in the live JS graph roots it, a GC pass collects it and PromiseHandlerTracker::discard with DiscardReason::kPromiseCollected emits this exact string. That callback is the only producer of it in the file. In ProtocolPromiseHandler::add the handler chains onto the ORIGINAL promise when the value is a promise, so the weakly-held object is literally the test's new Promise(...). Upstream V8 main has since made makeWeak lazy, but that redesign is absent from 15.0-lkgr and 15.1-lkgr as well, so every Chromium through 151 has this shape. Reviewer verified all of the above independently by fetching the sources.

REMEDY: accepted limit, no code change now, which the bead names as one of its three permitted outcomes. This is an upstream weak-handle design that any awaitPromise caller hits, at loads this suite never runs at. Criterion 2 is satisfied by there being no change to copy anywhere; there is also no existing shared helper being bypassed, since test/helpers/wait.js takes evalInContentScript as a parameter and documents that each file defines its own.
